identity.description:
D8 measure, phase 1: paired report, reviewer limit and cases subset (0.12.0)

D8 "measure", phase 1: the tooling for the passes measurement. Version 0.12.0. No eval with model calls ran for this change; every test uses the fake SDK client.

## What changes

- **Record sources (R1).** Each `stages.verifications[]` entry and each posted finding has `sources`: every `{reviewer, pass}` that raised a finding with that fingerprint, also the passes whose copy the dedup step dropped. A merged finding has the union of its group. Each reviewer query in `cost.queries` has `pass`, and each verifier or escalation query has `verification` (the index of its verification). All new fields are optional, so `explain` and the scorer read an older record as before.
- **Judge cache (R2).** Each eval repeat writes `<out>/<case>/<repeat>/judge-cache.json` with every match and extras judge answer, keyed by the judge model and the texts the judge saw. A scoring with the cache asks no question twice.
- **Paired report (R3).** `pr-review eval --paired` adds a paired section: for each case and repeat, and for each repeat over all cases, the one-pass set and the all set, each with raw recall, posted recall, strict precision and cost; the same for each reviewer that ran more than one pass; the added goldens, the added false findings, the added cost per added golden, and the mean and spread of the paired differences over the repeats. `pr-review eval-report --cases <dir> --out <dir>` makes the same report from an earlier `--out` with no model call. A pair with no cached answer counts as no match, and the report prints a "Not valid" line for that repeat.
- **Reviewer limit (R4).** `eval --reviewers history,tests --passes history=2,tests=2` runs only the named reviewers (they still need the normal selection) with the passes set for the run. A pass that `--passes` adds gets the same turn budget as any other pass. Unknown names, `--passes` with `--tier fast`, and either option with `--baseline` or `--write-baseline` are usage errors (exit 2). Both options go into `result.json`, so `--resume` refuses a run with other values.
- **Subset (R5).** `pr-review eval-subset --cases <dir> --costs <report.json | out dir | baseline> (--max-cost <usd> | --budget <usd> --repeats <n>) --to <dir>` copies the kept cases and writes the limit, the source and the costs into the new directory.
- **Baseline cost per case (R6).** `--write-baseline` writes `case_costs`. The reader accepts a baseline without it, so `eval/baseline.json` stays valid.

## What an old record gives

A record from before 0.12.0 has no source fields. The paired report lists each such repeat under "missing" with the reason "no source fields" and gives no figures for it; the command does not fail. The `--out` directory of the D4b baseline run no longer exists, so its cost per case and its records are in no file. Phase 2 takes the subset from the measured cost of its own first repeat, as agreed with the principal.

## Limits

The one-pass set filters the posted findings of the two-pass run. It does not model the merge or the cap that a one-pass run would form. The one-pass cost keeps the triage, merge and severity queries whole.

## Spec

The spec of this PR is the D8 entry of TICKETS.md ("Measurement design"), phase 1, with these requirements: R1 the record links each finding and query to its pass; R2 the eval keeps every judge answer; R3 the paired report, live and offline; R4 a run limited to named reviewers with passes set for the run; R5 a cases subset by cost; R6 cost per case in the baseline. Non-goals: the measurement run, the research note and the passes default (phase 2); a reviewer or passes option on `pr-review review`.

## Decisions

- Change path, not investigation. Not the light path: the record and baseline data shapes change (band deep).
- The principal agreed: the record changes are in scope; the baseline keeps the cost per case from the next `--write-baseline`; phase 2 takes its subset from the measured cost of its first repeat.
- Names chosen (reversible): `eval --paired`, `eval-report`, `eval-subset`, `--reviewers`, `--passes`.
- A merge that fails or that code rejects posts each member with its own sources, so a pass-2-only finding stays out of the one-pass set.
- The judge cache also keeps `unknown` answers, so the offline report equals the live scoring.
- `eval-subset` copies the kept cases: the case loader skips linked directories.

## Checks

`npm test` (1464 tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` pass. The new tests fail at the red commit d45a51c (20 failed).

triage.summary: Adds measurement tooling for comparing one reviewer pass against all passes. The run record now links each finding and each query to its reviewer pass. Eval gains --paired, --reviewers and --passes, a per-repeat judge cache, and two new commands: eval-report (rescoring with no model call) and eval-subset (a cases subset by cost). The baseline now stores case_costs, and the version moves to 0.12.0.

finding.claim: eval-report joins the record name from result.json to the repeat directory and does not check it, so a crafted result.json can make it read a file outside the --out directory.

finding.explanation: The `record` field is any string, so a value such as `../../x.json` can reach outside the repeat directory.

first.rationale: The result.json `record` field is an unchecked string. It goes straight into `join(dir, name)`, so `../` can leave the repeat directory. Only a file that parses as a RecordSchema record is used, and the user passes `--out` themselves. Impact is limited to an odd file read or a parse-error message, so this is a low-severity hardening point.

escalated.rationale: The claim is true: `result.record` can be any string, and `readRecord` joins it to the directory without checking it, so `../` can point outside. The risk is very small, though. Anyone who can write result.json can already put a record file in the --out directory. Also, the file it reads must pass `RecordSchema`, and only metrics come out. So this gives no real access to data.

final.rationale: The claim is true: `result.record` can be any string, and `readRecord` joins it to the directory without checking it, so `../` can point outside. The risk is very small, though. Anyone who can write result.json can already put a record file in the --out directory. Also, the file it reads must pass `RecordSchema`, and only metrics come out. So this gives no real access to data.

findings.claim: The description says each judge answer is keyed by the judge model and the texts the judge saw, but the extras key holds only the posted finding text, not the span, diff or policy the judge also sees.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the span, diff and policy texts in the key, or change the description to say what the key holds.
findings.explanation: A change of the span, the diff or the policy reuses a stale cached answer, which goes against the stated key.

quotes:
* the texts of the question. The match judge gives the posted finding and
 * the golden finding. The extras judge gives the posted finding.
verifier.rationale: The finding is correct. The extras key hashes only the describePosted text, while the judge also sees the span window, the diff and the policy, so the description's "keyed by the texts the judge saw" is loose. Each cache belongs to one repeat with a fixed head and diff, and the code comment in judge-cache.ts states what the key really holds, so a stale answer could come only from a policy or prompt edit between runs. That makes this a minor wording point.
